faq.q: What is the entry post of the BCS Customs and Excise cadre?
faq.a: Assistant Commissioner (Customs and Excise) at the National Board of Revenue, at Grade 9, following BCS entry grades.

faq.q: What is the salary of a BCS Customs officer?
faq.a: Under the new 9th pay scale the Grade 9 basic is listed at BDT 44,000 (old scale BDT 22,000), paid in stages up to July 2027, plus allowances. Check the gazette for exact figures and for the grade of each rank.

faq.q: Where do new customs officers train?
faq.a: At CEVTA, the Customs, Excise and VAT Training Academy in Chattogram, set up in 1981. BSS reported in September 2025 that cadre foundation training was cut from six to four months.

faq.q: What does a customs officer actually do?
faq.a: Assesses duty and value, checks declarations, runs post-clearance audits, works on intelligence and anti-smuggling, and helps honest trade clear quickly at ports and borders.

faq.q: What is happening to the NBR?
faq.a: An ordinance in May 2025 abolished the NBR and created Revenue Policy and Revenue Management Divisions, amended in September 2025 after protests. In April 2026 it faced a deadline to go before Parliament, and we could not confirm the final position, so check current news.

faq.q: How many Customs and Excise posts are advertised?
faq.a: We could not confirm the 50th BCS number, so check the circular. A coaching-centre table for the 45th BCS listed about 54, which is only indicative.

faq.q: Do I need a commerce or law degree?
faq.a: It is a general cadre, so any recognised bachelor's degree usually qualifies. Economics, commerce and law help, but check the circular.

faq.q: Does BCS Customs need a CV?
faq.a: BCS does not choose by CV, and marks decide. A short honest profile helps in the viva and in backup applications. For example: 'Economics graduate preparing for the BCS general cadre, with a study on port delays and experience managing a club budget.'

body_md:
**By [Daloyar Hassan Shishir](https://www.dhshishir.com)** · Career consultant, founder of Career Solutions and HereWeGrow · Facts last checked: 19 November 2026 · Last updated: 19 November 2026

> **Quick answer:** BCS (Customs and Excise) is the cadre that guards Bangladesh's borders and ports for revenue and trade. New officers join the National Board of Revenue (NBR) as Assistant Commissioner (Customs and Excise) at Grade 9, train at the Customs, Excise and VAT Training Academy (CEVTA) in Chattogram, and are posted to customs houses, commissionerates and intelligence and audit units. The cadre uses the same BCS exam as every general cadre (200-mark preliminary, 900-mark written, 100-mark viva). Customs brought in about 27 per cent of NBR revenue in FY2024-25, so the work matters. Under the new 9th pay scale the Grade 9 basic pay is listed at BDT 44,000, phased in up to July 2027. The NBR's structure was disputed in 2025-26, so check it before you rank this cadre. We could not confirm the Customs and Excise post count for the 50th BCS.

## Key facts (as of 19 November 2026)

| Question | Answer | Source type |
|---|---|---|
| What is the entry post? | Assistant Commissioner (Customs and Excise) | NBR transfer-posting pages |
| Entry grade | Grade 9 | BCS entry-grade table |
| Starting basic pay | BDT 44,000 (new 9th scale, phased in to July 2027); old scale BDT 22,000 | Daily Star Bangla; teacher-portal summary |
| Where do new officers train? | CEVTA, Chattogram (set up in 1981) | CEVTA |
| Length of cadre foundation training | Cut from six to four months in Sept 2025 (three months at institutions, one in the field) | BSS |
| Customs share of NBR revenue | 27% in FY2024-25 | BSS; TBS |
| Customs revenue target FY2025-26 | BDT 1,30,780 crore of a BDT 5,00,300 crore NBR target | Bangladesh Monitor |
| Exam | Preliminary 200 MCQ, written 900, viva 100 | BPSC |
| 50th BCS size | 1,755 cadre posts; 290,951 applicants; Customs count not confirmed | bdnews24; Dhaka Times |

*Numbers can change with each circular. The BPSC circular and the gazette are the final authority.*

## What does a Customs and Excise officer do?

Customs officers check that goods entering and leaving the country are declared, valued and taxed correctly, stop smuggling and fake goods, and help honest trade move fast. The work covers:

- **Customs houses and ports.** Chattogram Customs House supports Chittagong Port and, by one Daily Star estimate, handles 70 to 80 per cent of customs revenue. Other customs houses and land ports include Dhaka, Benapole, Pangaon and Mongla.
- **Commissionerates.** Customs, Excise and VAT commissionerates in Dhaka and elsewhere run duty and VAT work.
- **Intelligence, audit and investigation.** Directorates and units that check post-clearance records and chase evasion. Customs seized 144,000 counterfeit items in a recent year, according to TBS.
- **Trade facilitation.** Customs now runs on ASYCUDA World, the Bangladesh Single Window (which links 19 agencies and has issued about 900,000 certificates and permits, per UNB) and automated risk management. A report citing a time-release study says about 90 per cent of consignments clear within a day.
- **NBR headquarters,** including First Secretary posts and policy work.

The Customs Act, 2023 and its rules are the core law. CEVTA's course for Assistant Commissioners is built around that Act.

## What is the NBR reform, and why does it matter to you?

The same restructuring that affects the Taxation cadre affects you.

- **12 May 2025:** an ordinance abolished the NBR and created a Revenue Policy Division and a Revenue Management Division. The management division would handle enforcement, audits and compliance for income tax, VAT and customs, while the policy division would draft laws, set rates and oversee tax treaties, according to The Daily Star.
- **Protests and amendment:** tax and customs cadre officers protested, and a 1 September 2025 amendment required the head of the management division to come from officials with revenue-collection experience (TBS).
- **April 2026:** Prothom Alo reported on 6 April that the ordinance had not yet been placed before Parliament and would lapse if not presented by 10 April 2026.
- **Today:** we could not confirm which structure is legally in force. Check the latest news and the circular.

Whatever happens, ports and borders will still need customs officers.

## What is the career ladder?

| Rank | Notes |
|---|---|
| Assistant Commissioner (Customs and Excise) | Entry post for the BCS cadre at Grade 9 |
| Deputy Commissioner | Promotion from Assistant Commissioner |
| Joint Commissioner | |
| Additional Commissioner | |
| Commissioner | Often heads a customs house or commissionerate |
| Member (Customs) and above | Senior NBR posts |

*The rank names come from NBR's transfer-posting pages. We have not verified the pay grade attached to each rank, so check the gazette for grades.*

Alongside the BCS cadre, the department has Revenue Officers and Assistant Revenue Officers who rise from within. As in tax, promotion timelines depend on vacancies and the rules, so do not count on a fixed number of years.

## How many Customs and Excise posts are there, and how hard is it?

We could not find the Customs and Excise post count for the 50th BCS in the sources we checked. A coaching-centre table for the 45th BCS lists 54 posts for this cadre, which is only indicative. The NBR announced a customs and VAT expansion creating 3,597 new posts, including 373 cadre posts and 3,224 non-cadre posts (bdnews24), so future circulars may carry more cadre posts, but check the actual numbers.

| Exam | Total cadre posts | Applicants |
|---|---|---|
| 47th BCS | 3,487 advertised; 1,320 recommended | 374,747 |
| 50th BCS | 1,755 | 290,951 |

In the 50th BCS, 12,385 passed the preliminary and 6,165 passed the written exam (result published 23 July 2026). Allocation depends on your merit position, your cadre choices and the vacancies.

## What happens in training?

- **CEVTA, Chattogram.** Established in 1981 under the NBR to give foundation training to customs and VAT staff. It offers specialised foundation training for BCS (Customs and Excise) officers.
- **Course content.** The Assistant Commissioner course covers the Customs Act, 2023 and its rules and notifications. Revenue Officers also study the VAT and Supplementary Duty Act, 2012.
- **Foundation training length.** The National Training Council cut cadre foundation training from six to four months in September 2025, with three months in institutions and one month in the field. Check what applies to your batch.
- **Modernisation.** The government plans a new Customs House and Customs Academy in Chattogram with World Bank financing, according to a Dhaka Courier report.

## What is the salary and what are the benefits?

The 9th National Pay Scale was approved by cabinet on 31 August 2026 and takes effect from 1 July 2026. Basic pay is raised in stages up to July 2027, so early pay is below the final figure. Allowances are reset from January 2028.

| Grade | Old basic (BDT) | New basic (BDT) |
|---|---|---|
| 9 (Assistant Commissioner entry) | 22,000 | 44,000 |
| 6 | 35,500 | 71,000 |
| 5 | 43,000 | 86,000 |
| 3 | 56,500 | 1,13,000 |
| 2 | 66,000 | 1,32,000 |
| 1 | 78,000 | 1,56,000 |

*Source note: these figures come from a teacher-portal summary of the new scale, not the gazette. The Daily Star Bangla separately confirms Grade 1 at BDT 1,56,000. We have not matched each customs rank to a grade, so check the gazette.*

**Benefits beyond basic pay** (check your appointment terms): house rent and medical allowance, festival bonuses, leave and pension under government rules. In January 2026 the NBR chairman said improving housing for customs officials and staff was a commitment, so housing at ports is an area to ask about.

## Which skills does a customs officer need?

| Skill | Why it matters | Demand |
|---|---|---|
| Customs law and procedure | Customs Act, 2023, rules and notifications | █████ |
| Trade, valuation and goods classification | Correct duty depends on value and classification | █████ |
| Integrity and resisting pressure | Large sums, fast-moving cargo | █████ |
| Intelligence and investigation | Misdeclaration, smuggling, fake goods | ████ |
| Digital systems | ASYCUDA, Single Window, risk management | ████ |
| Official writing | Orders, seizure reports | ███ |
| Communication with traders | Hearings and facilitation | ███ |
| Numbers and economics | Duty calculations and trade patterns | ███ |

*Bars show our reading of the role, not a survey.*

## How do I get in? The exam path

Customs and Excise uses the general BCS exam: a 200-mark MCQ preliminary, a 900-mark written exam (Bangla 200, English 200, Bangladesh Affairs 200, International Affairs 100, Mathematical Reasoning and Mental Ability 100, General Science and Technology 100) and a 100-mark viva. See our BCS overview for the full guide.

**To aim for Customs and Excise:**

1. Put it on your cadre list only if the work interests you, and add realistic second and third choices.
2. Learn the basics of import-export: what a bill of entry is, how duty is calculated, what a port does.
3. Build maths and economics early.
4. Follow the customs reform news (Single Window, port clearance) and the NBR structure story.
5. Practise written answers on trade and governance.
6. Keep a plan B.

## Where will you find more peace of mind?

No cadre is free of pressure, and we have no survey to rank them. Customs work sits where traders, ports and deadlines meet. The Daily Star has reported that the Anti-Corruption Commission often examines revenue-evasion allegations against customs house officers, while traders accuse the house of harassment. A career here rewards clean, documented decisions and a calm manner. Three habits protect your peace: record every decision, keep a clear distance from favours, and stay close to colleagues you can talk to honestly.

## Plan your own path (5-minute worksheet)

Copy these lines and fill them in today:

1. **My age on the next cut-off date:** ___ (must be 32 or under)
2. **My cadre choices:** 1) Customs and Excise 2) ___ 3) ___
3. **My comfort with trade and numbers (score out of 10):** ___
4. **Three weakest subjects:** ___, ___, ___
5. **Daily practice minutes (writing and maths):** ___ (aim for 90)
6. **My plan B if I do not get a cadre:** ___

Then take the free skill test on this page and compare the result with line 4.

## Faith and history: honest measure

**The Quran.** Surah Al-Mutaffifin 83:1-3 warns against those who take full measure from others but give less when they measure or weigh for them ([read it on quran.com](https://quran.com/83/1-3)). It speaks to fair trade and honest dealing.

**Hadith.** The Prophet (peace be upon him) said that whoever cheats us is not one of us (Sahih Muslim 101). For a customs officer, this applies equally to a trader's false declaration and to an officer's own shortcuts.

**History.** International Customs Day is observed on 26 January, and CEVTA was set up in 1981 to train customs and VAT officers in Chattogram.

## Your contribution to the nation

Customs protects local industry from fake and dangerous goods, collects revenue that pays for public services and helps honest importers and exporters move quickly. A customs officer who clears an honest exporter's shipment on time supports jobs, and one who stops a dangerous import protects families.

## Your contribution to the world

Customs works with international partners on trade facilitation, counterfeit goods and border security. Officers can build skills through World Customs Organization programmes and study trade policy abroad, and many move into trade and development work.

## If you do not get BCS Customs and Excise

- **Other BCS cadres.** The same exam leads to Taxation, Administration, Police, Audit and Accounts and more.
- **Departmental route.** The NBR has Assistant Revenue Officer and Revenue Officer posts through separate recruitment. Check current circulars.
- **Trade and logistics careers.** Clearing and forwarding firms, shipping lines, ports and supply chain companies.
- **Private and development jobs** in trade compliance and logistics.

## Research opportunities

- Topics with real need: trade facilitation, time-release studies, risk management, port performance, counterfeit goods and the effects of customs digitalisation.
- Where to learn: economics, international business and law departments, trade think tanks, CEVTA.
- Path: a strong master's thesis, a research assistant post, then MPhil or PhD.

## Whom to follow and learn from

Follow institutions: [BPSC](https://www.bpsc.gov.bd), the [National Board of Revenue](https://nbr.gov.bd) and [CEVTA](https://cevta.gov.bd). Treat coaching centre promises and social media rank claims with caution.

## Where do I find circulars?

- BPSC's official site: [bpsc.gov.bd](https://www.bpsc.gov.bd).
- Teletalk's BPSC application portal: bpsc.teletalk.com.bd.
- Daily newspapers' job pages (cross-check every date and number with the circular).

**No lobbying.** Tadbir during the application process is treated as grounds for disqualification.

## How should I write my profile and CV?

BCS does not choose candidates from a CV. Marks decide. A short, honest profile helps in the viva and in backup applications.

| Weak line | Better line |
|---|---|
| Interested in trade. | Wrote a 15-page study on Chattogram port delays and presented it at a university seminar. |
| Honest and responsible. | Managed a BDT 2 lakh club budget and published a full account to all members. |
| Good with numbers. | Scored 85% in economics and built a spreadsheet comparing import duties for 10 goods. |

*Use only real, provable figures.*

Build yours free with the HereWeGrow CV Builder.

## What are the common mistakes?

- Choosing Customs without understanding port life and the integrity pressure.
- Ignoring maths and basic trade ideas.
- Skipping written practice.
- Treating the viva as a place for memorised answers.
- Having no plan B.
- Believing rumours about marks or posts instead of the circular.

## Changelog

- **19 Nov 2026:** First version. Customs and Excise post count for the 50th BCS not found; NBR structure after April 2026 not confirmed. Both flagged in the text.
- Next planned review: when the 52nd BCS circular is published or the NBR structure is settled.

cv_template_notes: BCS does not select by CV, so use a clean one-page academic-style HWG layout (single column, no heavy graphics) for your viva profile, backup applications and scholarships. Lead with education and results, then economics, commerce or law coursework, internships, volunteering and any research on trade. Add real numbers (budgets managed, hours served, scores). cover_letter_md:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the [position] advertised on [site/date]. I hold a [degree] from [university] and have strong analytical, numerical and writing skills built while preparing for the BCS Customs and Excise cadre. In [project/volunteering role] I [one provable result, e.g. managed a BDT 2 lakh club budget and published a full account to all members].

My CV is attached as a PDF. I would be glad to attend an interview.

Sincerely,
[Your name] | [Phone] | [Email]

(Note: BCS itself needs no cover letter. Use this for backup non-BCS applications.)
interview_qs: Why do you want to join the Customs and Excise cadre? (Tip: Give a real reason from experience; talk about trade, revenue and border protection, not status.)
What does an Assistant Commissioner of Customs do? (Tip: Mention assessing duty, checking declarations, audit, anti-smuggling and trade facilitation.)
Why does customs matter for Bangladesh's economy? (Tip: Revenue share (about 27% of NBR), protecting industry, trade speed.)
What is the difference between a tariff and a non-tariff barrier? (Tip: Tariff is a duty; non-tariff covers permits, quotas and standards; give one example each.)
What would you do if a powerful importer pressured you to clear goods without checks? (Tip: Follow the law, document, inform your superior, stay polite.)
What is your view on the NBR split into policy and management divisions? (Tip: Show you know both sides: reform goals and officers' concerns; stay calm and neutral.)
How can technology improve customs clearance? (Tip: Single Window, risk management, scanners; mention fairness and data security.)
Traders complain of delays at Chattogram port. How would you respond? (Tip: Listen, check the process, find the real bottleneck, avoid blaming.)
What is the difference between smuggling and misdeclaration? (Tip: Smuggling avoids customs entirely; misdeclaration lies about goods or value; both break the law.)
Why not Taxation or another cadre? (Tip: Show you know the other cadre; explain your fit with Customs.)
How do you handle revenue-target pressure? (Tip: Stay lawful; focus on accurate assessment and compliance, not shortcuts.)
Are you ready to work at a port or border posting far from home? (Tip: Be honest; show readiness and a practical plan for family and health.)
Describe a time you handled money or records honestly. (Tip: Situation, action, result in numbers if possible.)
What will you do if you are not selected this time? (Tip: Show a calm plan B; do not sound defeated.)
Do you have any questions for us? (Tip: Ask about training or learning, not about pay or posting.)
